data.title: Unloved Stocks Rally as AI Trade Loses Steam
data.description: According to CNBC, the Nasdaq Composite is down 2.7% in 2026 and has fallen 14% over the past month as the AI trade lost steam, while several out-of-favor non-AI stocks advanced. The Campbell's Company rose nearly 20% over the past month, even though only one of 23 analysts rates it a buy, FactSet data showed. BTIG chief market technician Jonathan Krinsky said low investor ownership and widespread lack of interest could set up the stock for a sharp move higher, with a potential trading-volume area near $30. Clorox also gained roughly 20% over the past month, despite analysts' average forecast for an 11% decline over the next 12 months. JetBlue Airways rose 14%; only one analyst rates the airline a buy, and it faces higher fuel costs. Boston Beer advanced nearly 13% after raising its full-year adjusted earnings guidance in October to $9 to $10.50 per share, above FactSet's $8.90 consensus estimate. Only 6.7% of analysts covering Boston Beer rate it a buy. Lululemon and Prudential Financial also appeared on the list of unpopular stocks that outperformed the broader market over the past month.

data.title: Anthropic's Record IPO Debut Coincides With Tech's Worst Week on Wall Street Since 2020
data.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and secured an additional $26 billion from technology companies that bought shares at the offering price. The stock rose 17% in its Thursday debut, giving the company a $1.8 trillion market capitalization. The debut came as technology shares suffered their worst week since 2020: Nvidia fell 23%, its sharpest weekly decline in 18 years, and the Nasdaq dropped 10% over the past five trading days.

data.title: Tech Outages Drive Surge in Emergency-Prep Spending
data.description: According to CNBC, spending at brands specializing in emergency products rose about 400% from a year earlier between Nov. 12 and Nov. 17, when at least half a dozen major technology outages occurred in the U.S. Ready America’s e-commerce sales increased roughly fivefold in recent days, and the company asked suppliers to increase production. Mizuho expects Costco’s non-fuel sales growth in November to top 10% for the first time since 2022, as shoppers stock up on emergency supplies. The Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) gained about 2.5% over the past two weeks, while the Nasdaq Composite fell into negative territory for 2026 on Friday.

data.title: Trump Rally Gains Fade as AI Investment Concerns Pressure U.S. Stocks and Crypto
data.description:
U.S. stocks and cryptocurrency markets sold off sharply this week amid concerns over AI investment and the fading of gains associated with U.S. President Donald Trump. According to Odaily, Bitcoin briefly fell below $56,000 for the first time since September 2024, erasing all gains since Trump won that year’s U.S. election. The total cryptocurrency market value has fallen about $2.3 trillion from its record high, with hundreds of billions of dollars flowing out in the past month alone.

U.S. stocks also came under pressure. The Nasdaq fell 5.3% on Friday, wiping out its gains for the year. The S&P 500 recorded its worst weekly performance since April 2025 and fell more than 10% from its October peak, entering correction territory.

Market analysts said the selloff began before Democrats regained control of the House and Senate and was driven mainly by concerns about large technology companies’ substantial AI investments. Since the S&P 500 reached a high on October 6, the estimated market value of U.S. stocks has declined by about $6 trillion. Analysts also said the Democratic victory may end the so-called “Trump Put”—the belief that Trump would step in to stabilize markets under pressure.

Technology analyst Dan Ives described the market environment as a “perfect storm,” citing investor concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress may be less supportive of the AI industry and data center construction. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s high-profile departure, investigations involving the company and the possibility of further Federal Reserve rate hikes have also unsettled markets. The selloff is still viewed as a market correction, and Ives said his long-term view of AI had not changed.

data.title: BTCS Discloses to SEC That $54 Million Aave Loan Faces Liquidation Risk
data.description:
BTCS disclosed to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that its approximately $54 million Aave loan, backed by ETH, could be liquidated. According to Odaily, the Nasdaq-listed company said in a filing that it cannot guarantee future borrowing levels or collateral values, or that liquidation will not occur.

As of November 19, BTCS owed about $54 million on Aave, down roughly $10 million from about $64 million two weeks earlier. The value of its collateral has remained under pressure as ETH prices fell. CoinDesk estimated that, assuming the company still holds the previously disclosed 46,676 ETH as collateral, the loan’s health factor is about 1.2; the position could face liquidation if ETH falls below approximately $1,450. BTCS said the borrowing primarily supports liquidity pools for its Imperium business.

BTCS shares fell 12.2% on Friday to close at $0.653, bringing their weekly decline to 28.1%.

data.title: White House Plans to Scale Back Special Government Employee Use, Including Elon Musk and Former Crypto Adviser David Sacks
data.description:
The White House plans to reduce its use of Special Government Employees (SGEs), a designation that lets private-sector personnel work for the government while retaining private-sector compensation or investment income. According to Odaily, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller has told associates he wants to phase out the designation, and several prominent SGEs have left or are leaving government teams in recent weeks.

SGEs are rarely required to disclose client information or conflicts of interest. Federal rules limit their government work to 130 days a year, though that cap can be extended if needed.

Prominent former SGEs include businessman Elon Musk, who previously led the Department of Government Efficiency; Corey Lewandowski, a former senior adviser at the Department of Homeland Security; and technology entrepreneur David Sacks, who previously oversaw artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency matters. All three have left government service.

The White House does not plan to ban the designation but intends to use it cautiously, two people familiar with the matter said. A White House official said Miller favors prioritizing full-time hires and plans to crack down on what he considers misuse of the SGE status.

data.title: Kalshi Institutional Trading Volume Rises 4,124% in Six Months to $26.3 Billion in October
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Fortune and Ticker Tracker, institutional trading volume on Kalshi rose 4,124% in six months, from $622.7 million in April to $26.3 billion in October. The number of institutional accounts trading on the platform increased from 312 to 822, with 242 recording more than $1 million in monthly volume.

The figures exclude perpetual futures, market makers, designated liquidity providers and internal accounts. Most of the $26.3 billion came from regular order-book trading rather than negotiated block trades. Ticker Tracker data show that in the 30 days through November 20, sports and parlay contracts accounted for about 85% of Kalshi’s trading volume, while financial and economic contracts combined made up less than 1%. The data cover all traders, not just institutions.

data.title: Crypto Rover Says Bitcoin Is Testing 300- and 350-Week Averages, a Historical Bottoming Zone
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Crypto Rover said Bitcoin is testing its 300-week and 350-week moving averages, which he described as a historical buying zone and long-term support during deep corrections. Bitcoin found support near these levels in 2015, 2020 and 2022 before rallying significantly. Rover added that despite current market fear, history suggests the zone has offered opportunities for long-term accumulation.

data.title: Bitcoin Long Liquidation Cluster Between $59,000 and $62,000 Cleared
data.description: A dense cluster of Bitcoin long liquidations between $59,000 and $62,000 was completely cleared yesterday. According to Odaily, Glassnode said it had been tracking the cluster and that its removal eliminated a major source of forced selling below Bitcoin’s price.

data.title: FBI Investigates Suspected Hack of Criminal Information Database
data.description: According to CNBC, the FBI is investigating a suspected breach of the National Crime Information Center, a nationwide database used by federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share criminal justice information. CNN reported Friday, citing two people briefed on the investigation, that the database was apparently compromised. It stores and shares information on warrants, criminal histories and background checks.

data.title: LART Raises $2.5 Million in Funding With IBC Group and Others Participating
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, LART, an art-recovery and RWA tokenization protocol, has completed a $2.5 million funding round, with participation from IBC Group, x21 Digital, Genesis Capital VC, and GaeaVentures. Built on BNB Smart Chain, the protocol aims to recover lost artworks, record their provenance on-chain, and bring physical art into a regulated RWA framework.
